subject.title: fix(infra): fix exec-approvals async lock, not just the sync path (#106777, extends #108971)

question: Should exec approvals keep a bespoke local nonce lock for its authorization boundary, or should the shared `@openclaw/fs-safe` sidecar lock be corrected and consumed as the single implementation?
rationale: Both paths can address the reported VirtioFS identity failure, but choosing a local authorization-specific lock versus repairing the shared dependency determines long-term ownership, divergence, and the scope of security review.

options.title: Repair the shared lock contract
options.body: Move the proven nonce-ownership fix into the shared lock implementation, update the dependency path, and retain exec-approvals-specific fail-closed policy tests.

options.title: Approve an exec-approvals-specific lock
options.body: Keep the local implementation only with an explicit rationale for why authorization policy needs distinct ownership and with focused proof that all callback paths preserve the documented atomicity invariant.

recommendation.title: Repair the shared lock contract
recommendation.body: Move the proven nonce-ownership fix into the shared lock implementation, update the dependency path, and retain exec-approvals-specific fail-closed policy tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The related nonce-lock proposal is the clearest available history signal for the implementation direction under review.
